chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Ja‘far al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn ibn Abī al-Khaṭṭāb, from Ṣafwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Mālik al-Juḥanī, from Abū ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allāh assigned to al-Ḥusayn (peace be upon him) an angel, accompanied by four thousand angels, who weep for him, seek forgiveness for his visitors, and supplicate to Allāh for them.

key_terms.الْحُسَيْنِ: Al-Husayn, the grandson of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: What role do angels play in relation to Imam al-Husayn and his visitors according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cosmic dimension of Imam al-Ḥusayn’s (a.s.) martyrdom, illustrating that his spiritual authority extends beyond the earthly realm into the celestial court. The weeping of the four thousand angels serves as a divine endorsement of the Ziyārah ritual, linking the physical act of visiting his shrine with continuous intercession and forgiveness granted by the heavenly host.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 15. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Safwān ibn Yaḥyā, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Mālik Al-Juhani, who said: Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said:
Allāh has dedicated an angel (named Mansūr) along with four thousand angels to Ḥusain (a.s.). They cry over him and seek forgiveness for those who go to his Ziyārah and pray for them.
